issue_context.title: Add a keytab field to the Spark connection (handle the base64 encoded text value as a credential).
issue_context.body:
### Description

Hello,

I would like to introduce and propose a feature I have personally implemented in the SparkSubmitHook for managing Spark connections.

This feature focuses on managing the Kerberos-related principal and keytab within the connection settings.

The basic idea is to store the keytab as a base64 encoded credential. When submitting a Spark job, the credential is decoded and saved as a file, and its path is specified during the submission.

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1d242cd5-0484-4057-9159-4212862253ae)

### Use case/motivation

Setting up the keytab for each worker can be challenging, and managing the keytab each time it changes can be cumbersome. By storing this information within the connection, we can reduce the need to deploy the keytab every time.

I would appreciate your consideration of this proposal.

Thank you.

### Related issues

_No response_

review_comments: What with add test to this exception?
Is there a reason you added here `.{_uuid}`?
Yeah! This part was added to assign a unique staging_path to prevent concurrency issues that can occur with the same principal.
I was considering comparing the checksums for this part, but I'd appreciate your opinion on it
Why would it exist if only a few lines ago you created this path?
This logic exists to prevent writing the same file in the same execution environment each time.
So why do you move the file from staging to `keytab_path`?

After considering the scenarios where a read might occur during a write operation or a write might fail or some concurrency cases, I thought that it would be safest to write to a staging file successfully first and then move it.

Additionally, the cases where writing occurs are when the keytab is not present at the path or when the contents of the keytab at the path have changed.
Got it, so maybe just add to the comment `#write new keytab file`, why you're creating a new keytab.
added the detailed reason as a comment, thanks!
Also what with add test to this exception? What if it fails to write to the file or copy it with `shutil.move` we don't want there to be a test on it?
